ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this dispute is over trip TRP-02802, Northpoint City to Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4.

To the rider — your claim is substantially upheld. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the GPS trace figure of 14.56 km (EV-GPS-02802), not the rounded 14.6 km convenience copy on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 11.4 km and 15.4 minutes (EV-TRIP-02802) the excess is 3.16 km, or 27.72% of optimal. That clears both establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 115 fixes, a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires and the deviation stands on the trace alone with no independent corroboration required.

To the driver — your explanation that traffic was heavy so you took another road does not assist you. Under POL-RD-13 an asserted external traffic cause is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02802-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no advisory is on file, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. You named no advisory evidence ID, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than the contradiction that would escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5), and the deviation stands at the measured figure. Your statement that the fare is what the meter says does not change this: the meter is derived from the same trace.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which applies because the fare model is METERED (EV-FARE-02802). Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 × 11.4 optimal km + 0.28 × 15.4 optimal min) × 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 waiting time − 0.00 promo = 17.4620. State the three figures separately: charged_total = 20.87; recomputed_fare = 17.4620; refund = 3.4080, rounded UP to SGD 3.45. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share of charged_total (18.783), so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.45.

No other clause adds anything. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02802) carries zero messages, so there is no rider-requested detour or additional stop to exonerate distance under POL-RD-04. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment (original points, amendment timestamps and amended optimal all null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not displace the booked optimal. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, so POL-RD-09 makes no pass-through correction and there is no billing-integrity defect. The driver's profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 295 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 establishes no repeat pattern and produces neither a full-refund uplift nor a conduct referral; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field that clause names and was given no weight. The rider's 60-day deviation-claim counters are 0, so no extra corroboration is required under POL-RD-08; the rider's other profile fields (prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding.

Confidence is 0.9. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — sits at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no confidence discount applies and no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The monetary effect of SGD 3.45 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes automatically on issue.

Audit note: two driver-side claims were discarded by the referee for citing the MISSING advisory EV-ADVIS-02802-01 at weight 0.0 without naming its issue code (MISSING_ARTIFACT).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
